scenes.tts: How fast can one living cell destroy a protein? Chapter one ended with the brake lifting. The A P C tagged securin, and the proteasome destroyed it. Now, how can you read that speed?
scenes.caption: How fast can one living cell destroy a protein? Chapter 1 ended with the brake lifting. The APC/C tagged securin, and the proteasome destroyed it. Now, how can you read that speed?
scenes.visual: Open on chapter 1's world, mid-action, filling about 70% of frame height: the flat PtK1-style mitotic cell (wide ellipse) with grey spindle poles left and right, yellow sister-chromatid pairs lined up on the middle line, every white kinetochore attached, no red ring, the red wire dark. Upper right, the ENGINE: blue 'APC/C' with teal 'Cdc20', its notches empty. A purple 'securin' docks, gains a chain of small gold ubiquitin tags, slides into the grey barrel 'proteasome' and comes out as fading fragments. More purple securins sit in a loose cluster beside the engine and keep docking one by one, not all at once. The cycle track along the bottom shows the white marker sitting at 'metaphase'. On 'How fast can one living cell destroy a protein' a gold question card slides in at the upper left: 'How fast?'
scenes.narration: How fast can one living cell destroy a protein? Chapter 1 ended with the brake lifting. The APC/C tagged securin, and the proteasome destroyed it. Now, how can you read that speed?

scenes.visual: Title over the same cell, which keeps breathing (slow 2% scale pulse) while securins keep trickling into the proteasome: 'Timing Securin's Destruction'.

scenes.tts: Tag securin with a fluorescent protein, and film a single cell. The glow tracks how much securin is left. In human HeLa cells, it starts to fall at metaphase, once the checkpoint is satisfied.
scenes.caption: Tag securin with a fluorescent protein, and film a single cell. The glow tracks how much securin is left. In human HeLa cells, it starts to fall at metaphase, once the checkpoint is satisfied.
scenes.visual: Tag top-left changes to 'HeLa cell (schematic)'; the cell outline stays in place. Every purple securin gains a small bright green halo (label 'securin + fluorescent tag'). The whole cell glows a soft green in proportion to how many tagged securins remain. A vertical gauge appears at the right edge, 'glow = securin left', reading 100%. The marker reaches 'metaphase', the last kinetochore is already attached, and only then do the tagged securins start docking at the APC/C and vanishing; the cell's green glow and the gauge begin to drop together.
scenes.narration: Tag securin with a fluorescent protein, and film a single cell. The glow tracks how much securin is left. In human HeLa cells, it starts to fall at metaphase, once the checkpoint is satisfied.

scenes.tts: Here are made-up numbers, for practice. At metaphase, one hundred percent. Five minutes later, seventy-one. Ten minutes, fifty. Fifteen minutes, thirty-five.
scenes.caption: Here are made-up numbers, for practice. At metaphase, 100 percent. Five minutes later, 71. Ten minutes, 50. Fifteen minutes, 35.
scenes.visual: The cell shrinks to the left third of the frame (still glowing, still trickling securin into the proteasome). On the right two thirds, axes draw themselves: x 'minutes after metaphase' 0 to 30, y 'securin glow (% of metaphase)' 0 to 100. Label at top of the axes, size 28, full opacity: 'made-up data'. As each value is spoken, the gauge beside the cell drops to it and a purple dot lands on the axes: (0, 100), (5, 71), (10, 50), (15, 35). The x axis from 15 to 30 is still empty.
scenes.narration: Here are made-up numbers, for practice. At metaphase, 100 percent. Five minutes later, 71. Ten minutes, 50. Fifteen minutes, 35.

scenes.tts: Treat this as exponential loss, with no new securin made. At ten minutes, half is gone. That time is the half-life. For exponential loss, a half-life removes half of what remains. The loss is a steady fraction, not a steady amount.
scenes.caption: Treat this as exponential loss, with no new securin made. At 10 minutes, half is gone. That time is the half-life. For exponential loss, a half-life removes half of what remains. The loss is a steady fraction, not a steady amount.
scenes.visual: A purple 'new securin' chip and an incoming arrow appear by the cell, both crossed out in white: 'none made'. A smooth purple curve, computed as 100 x e^(-0.0693 t), draws itself near the four rounded dots from 0 to 15 minutes. A gold dashed line drops from the point (10, 50) to the x axis; a gold bracket from 0 to 10 labelled 'half-life = 10 min'. Then two small step markers on the curve: from 0 to 5 minutes and from 10 to 15 minutes, each labelled 'x 0.71' in gold, showing the same fraction lost per 5 minutes although the drop in points is bigger early on.
scenes.narration: Treat this as exponential loss, with no new securin made. At 10 minutes, half is gone. That time is the half-life. For exponential loss, a half-life removes half of what remains. The loss is a steady fraction, not a steady amount.

scenes.tts: Here is a test for you. Ten minutes took the glow from one hundred down to fifty. What will it read at twenty minutes?
scenes.caption: Here is a test for you. Ten minutes took the glow from 100 down to 50. What will it read at 20 minutes?
scenes.visual: The gold bracket from 0 to 10 pulses. A hollow purple ring appears on the x axis at 20 minutes with a dashed vertical line above it, no value. A gold question card slides in at upper right: 'Glow at 20 minutes?'
scenes.narration: Here is a test for you. Ten minutes took the glow from 100 down to 50. What will it read at 20 minutes?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Question card stays on screen. The cell at left keeps breathing and its glow flickers gently; the dashed line at 20 minutes shimmers. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Twenty-five percent, not zero. Two half-lives halve it twice. The first ten minutes lost fifty points; the next ten lost only twenty-five.
scenes.caption: 25 percent, not zero. Two half-lives halve it twice. The first 10 minutes lost 50 points; the next 10 lost only 25.
scenes.visual: A ghost straight line from (0, 100) through (10, 50) runs on to (20, 0), labelled 'steady amount: zero' in full-opacity white, then fades out. The purple curve continues from 15 to 20 and the hollow ring fills as a purple dot at (20, 25), labelled '25%'. A second gold bracket from 10 to 20 labelled 'half-life'. Two vertical gold arrows on the y axis compare the drops: '-50' for 0 to 10 minutes, '-25' for 10 to 20 minutes. The question card shrinks away.
scenes.narration: 25 percent, not zero. Two half-lives halve it twice. The first 10 minutes lost 50 points; the next 10 lost only 25.

scenes.tts: The curve has a formula. F of t equals F zero, times e to the minus k t. The rate constant k is the natural log of two, divided by the half-life. Here, k is about zero point zero six nine per minute.
scenes.caption: The curve has a formula. F(t) = F0 × e^(−kt). The rate constant k is ln 2 divided by the half-life. Here, k is about 0.069 per minute.
scenes.visual: Above the graph, the formula writes itself in large white type: 'F(t) = F0 × e^(−kt)'. Each symbol glows as it is named and an arrow links it to the graph: F0 to the dot at (0, 100), t to the x axis, F(t) to the dot at (20, 25). Below it: 'k = ln 2 / half-life', and the gold 'half-life = 10 min' bracket slides up into the formula; it resolves to 'k ≈ 0.069 per minute'. The curve stays drawn.
scenes.narration: The curve has a formula. F(t) = F0 × e^(−kt). The rate constant k is ln 2 divided by the half-life. Here, k is about 0.069 per minute.

scenes.tts: Each securin the proteasome destroys is gone for good. While none is made, the curve can only fall. That fall is the one-way step from chapter one, measured in minutes.
scenes.caption: Each securin the proteasome destroys is gone for good. While none is made, the curve can only fall. That fall is the one-way step from chapter 1, measured in minutes.
scenes.visual: The cell at left grows back to fill the left half. One tagged securin goes into the grey proteasome and leaves as fragments; its outline stays dashed and empty, as in chapter 1. A small white marker rides down the purple curve as the cell's glow dims in step with it. The one-way chevron from chapter 1 appears on the cycle track at 'metaphase', pointing forward.
scenes.narration: Each securin the proteasome destroys is gone for good. While none is made, the curve can only fall. That fall is the one-way step from chapter 1, measured in minutes.

scenes.tts: So read this exponential destruction curve by its half-life. Every half-life halves what is left. From that one number you get the rate, and predict when any level is reached.
scenes.visual: The whole world, calm: the glowing cell on the left with the engine and proteasome, the curve on the right. The gold half-life brackets tick along the x axis, 0 to 10, then 10 to 20, and at each tick the dot on the computed curve halves: 100, 50, 25. The cell's glow steps down in step. Everything settles; slow ambient breathing continues.
scenes.narration: So read this exponential destruction curve by its half-life. Every half-life halves what is left. From that one number you get the rate, and predict when any level is reached.

scenes.line: Every half-life halves what is left.
